Reacquaint and then let's talk about our "Refactor:" tasks in TODO.md
We currently have 8 tasks remaining and it's actually not clear to
me the tasks in each of those.

Currently there are many operations in vc-x1 we do by spawning jj
and I want to eliminate all of those, if possible. I assume that's
possible because I assume anything jj does we can do directly.

Based on title of todo #1 it reads to me that this task is going to use jj-lib
and "end subprocess spawning". But that is also #6 implies, although the
semi-colon details says "; the index-lock retry becomes ours"

Maybe #1 is the overarching task, so I'm confused, help!

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# Todo

This file contains near term tasks with a short description
and reference links to more details.

Intro paragraphs in `## Todo` and `## Bugs` should begin every
line with 1 leading space so they don't match the `^\d+\. `
pattern that locates numbered entries; 2 or 3 spaces also work.

## In Progress

When a `## Todo` item is picked up, its text moves here: the
problem overview and its list of things to do. That is followed
by the "plan" — a bulleted list of the development "ladder".
Each rung is prepended with its commit reference — a literal
`[[N]]` placeholder until the commit is pushed, then backfilled
to a real file-local `[[n]]` ref (same pattern as the chores
As-built rungs):
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-0 blah (done)
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-1 blah blah (current)
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-2 blah blah blah
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y close-out and validation

_No cycle currently in progress._

## Todo

 Entries are in **strict priority rank** — #1 highest,
 descending. Reprioritize by moving an entry, then
 `vc-x1 fix-todo --no-dry-run TODO.md` to renumber.
 The numbers are positional rank, not stable IDs — to refer
 to a Todo, name it by its **title** (a greppable mention;
 a numbered list item has no anchor to link to), not its
 number. Long-tail entries
 live in [todo-backlog.md](notes/todo-backlog.md). Use the
 [Prose Form in AGENTS.md](/AGENTS.md#prose-form); deeper
 detail goes in `notes/chores/chores-NN.md` design
 subsections (link via `[N]` ref).

1. **Refactor: typed jj facade → jj-lib in-process; end
   subprocess spawning.** Version-control operations are
   ~30 hand-rolled `run("jj", …)` spawns plus every
   mutation, with per-module private wrappers and raw-git
   vestiges in init — stderr parsing instead of typed
   errors, and jj's single-attempt index-lock acquisition
   (the push `bookmark-set` lock race in [bugs.md](notes/bugs.md))
   can't be retried where it fails. A multi-ladder program;

    `## Done` entries, and chores headers — all written
    while the work is in progress, i.e. before it lands.

    merge-based flow (e.g. Linux), the version a change
    ships under is only fixed when it merges into `main`,
    so the landing version can't be anticipated while the
    work is underway. Pervasive version-in-text is
    therefore fragile for any non-linear / multi-contributor
    workflow. Promoted from Ideas at 0.65.2-0; slated for
    the cycle after 0.65.2.
    - Open question: what identifies a cycle's commits if
      not a pre-assigned version?
      - Needs to be unique within some agreed upon domain.
        A contributors email address would do it, but also
        a UUID (short-version) for a contribution. I could
        imagine a UUID generated from the initial email/issue
        that and then "version number" schema appended to that.
    - Surfaces to update once the identifier is chosen:
      cycle-protocol.md (title shape, Numbering), AGENTS.md
      (commit-recording headers), and the `vc-x1` validators
      that parse `(X.Y.Z)` strings.
12. **sync follow-up: extract `move-bookmark` command.** The
    "put the bookmark / `@` where it belongs" step at the end
    of sync (reposition logic) is useful standalone — e.g. the
    t1B scenario where `main` is right but `@` isn't on it —
    and deserves an honestly-named command instead of a mode.
    - `vc-x1 move-bookmark` (name open): no fetch; move `@`
      (and optionally the bookmark) onto a target under the
      same safety rules as sync's reposition step.
    - Sync's final step becomes a call to the same logic.
    - Follow-up to the 0.67.0 single-mode sync cycle.
13. **sync follow-up: push preflight in-process; drop

# Refactor: typed jj facade → jj-lib in-process (2026-07-16)

The plan-and-design document for the jj refactor program.
Version-control operations are scattered hand-rolled
`run("jj", …)` spawns (~30 query sites plus every mutation)
with per-module private wrappers, plus raw-git vestiges in
init. Spawning means stderr parsing instead of typed errors,
and jj's single-attempt index-lock acquisition sits outside
our control — the push `bookmark-set` lock race [[1]] can't
be retried where it fails.

How this file works:

- Each stage below is a `##` section in execution order;
  each is roughly one `X.Y.Z` cycle. Section anchors are the
  durable way to reference a stage from TODO.md, chores, or
  bugs.md.
- This file owns the forward plan and design. When a stage
  ships, its `chores-NN.md` section records the commits and
  narrative as usual; the stage section here gets a one-line
  status link to that chores section — no duplication.
- The `## Todo` entry "Refactor: typed jj facade → jj-lib
  in-process; end subprocess spawning" in
  [TODO.md](../TODO.md) is the short pointer here.

Absorbed former Todos: "Dedup jj subprocess queries behind a
typed facade", "Split push.rs state machinery", "vc-x1 push:
validate body opens with an intro paragraph", "Make the bot
repo directory name configurable", "Terminology stragglers
from the work/bot sweep", "single-field `options_flags`
leaves → `value` field", "`por → dual` conversion",
"`validate-desc` / `fix-desc` por equalization".

100	## Stage: facade owns topology
101	
102	In progress at 0.75.0
103	([chores](chores/chores-14.md#refactor-facade-owns-topology)).
104	Repo resolution becomes facade state, not per-command
105	preludes.
106	
107	- `validate-desc` / `fix-desc` por equalization: replace the
108	  `other_repo_from_config` prelude in both
109	  (`validate_desc.rs:133`, `fix_desc.rs:152`) with
110	  scope-aware resolution that no-ops `Side::Bot` when
111	  absent; body unchanged. The 0.61.0 audit [[2]] called this
112	  the cheapest equalization and the prototype for the
113	  topology-from-config rule (topology from `default_scope`,
114	  not a flag); the remaining implementation gaps live in
115	  [[2]]'s `## Gap list`.
116	- Make the bot repo directory name configurable (not
117	  hardcoded `.claude`; decided 2026-07-15 the name need not
118	  be `.claude`; decided 2026-07-21 the new default is
119	  `.bot`). The literal is embedded across
120	  init/clone/push/sync, `claude_path()`, diagnostic /
121	  logging strings (`bm-track`'s `.claude(main)=no-jj`),
122	  ochid path semantics (`/.claude/<chid>`), the
123	  `~/.claude/projects/<path>` symlink, and docs;
124	  `.vc-config.toml` already records workspace paths — the
125	  natural home. Schema shape decided 2026-07-23: the
126	  symmetric `work = "/"` / `bot = "/.bot"` pair *replaces*
127	  `path`/`other-repo` (identical `[workspace]` block on both
128	  sides — nothing to cross-check); side detection by
129	  location, walking up from cwd via `find_workspace_root`
130	  (root → work, `<root>/<bot-dir>` → bot; was the deferred
131	  half of `0.41.1-6`'s title; design in
132	  [chores-08 Operations](chores/chores-08.md#operations));
133	  presence of `bot` is the dual-repo signal (replacing
134	  presence-of-`other-repo`); POR is `work = "/"` alone.
135	  - Migration decided 2026-07-23: none — the config records
136	    each workspace's actual bot dir, so existing workspaces
137	    keep `.claude` (`bot = "/.claude"`) and their
138	    `/.claude/<chid>` trailers keep resolving verbatim;
139	    `.bot` is the *new-init default only* — a
140	    recommendation, not a mandate.
141	  - Still open: the harness-controlled symlink location,
142	    and the harness's own `<project>/.claude`
143	    settings/skills dir — renaming the bot repo splits it
144	    from the vendor's dir (only bites a workspace that
145	    *chooses* a non-`.claude` dir).
146	- `config` command reshape (decided 2026-07-23 during the
147	  0.75.0-2 review): positional `work|bot|work,bot|<path>`
148	  target (default `work,bot`), print by default with
149	  `--validate` switching to check mode; validate covers both
150	  sides' files plus the identical-`[workspace]`-block
151	  invariant; `--home` retires; the user-home file stays
152	  load-bearing but is reachable only via an explicit
153	  `<path>`.
154	- Path grammar for `work` / `bot` (pinned 2026-07-23): ochid
155	  path syntax — a leading `/` is *the workspace root*
156	  (workspace-relative, never filesystem-absolute). `work` is
157	  exactly `"/"`; `bot` is `"/" + one path component`, no
158	  trailing slash (the bot repo sits directly under the root —
159	  side detection and the root walk assume it). The `bot`
160	  value doubles verbatim as the bot-side ochid prefix.
161	  Defined and *enforced* at 0.75.0-3 (pulled forward from the
162	  `-4` plan — no downside): every resolver rejects a
163	  non-`"/"` `work` or a malformed `bot` loudly, since either
164	  would otherwise be silently ignored or corrupt trailers.
165	  The `-4` `config --validate` reuses the same check as the
166	  human-facing report.
167	- Dual-mode preflight principle (decided 2026-07-23, "my
168	  opinion ATM"): an operation entering dual-repo mode
169	  verifies both repos' expected state up front — bot dir
170	  exists, both configs parse, `[workspace]` blocks identical
171	  — and on any finding it stops, prints everything known
172	  (both paths, both blocks), and changes nothing. Mid-flight
173	  surprises remain per-operation concerns (sync's
174	  stop-and-inspect, push's rollback); *entry* is gated at
175	  the one topology resolver the 0.75.0-3 sweep centralizes.
176	  The full every-invocation form (validate-bot everywhere)
177	  stays a separate Todo — it has per-invocation cost
178	  questions.
179	- Bisect note: the two repos rewind independently — checking
180	  out a pre-0.75.0-2 work commit pairs an old binary + old
181	  work config with the bot repo's *current* (new-form)
182	  config, so bot-side lookups fail with "missing
183	  workspace.path" (loud but cryptic; old binaries are
184	  immutable, this paragraph is the decoder). Within either
185	  repo every commit is functional — schema flips land
186	  atomically with the configs they read (the 0.75.0-2
187	  shape), and the per-rung cargo cycle keeps intentionally
188	  broken commits out of history.
189	
190	## Stage: repo registry
191	
192	Decided 2026-07-24 (during the 0.75.0-4 review). The
193	`[workspace]` block becomes a repo registry — stable names
194	mapped to locations — and the root-anchored path grammar
195	(leading `/` = workspace root, pinned at 0.75.0-3) is
196	dropped. Complements the URL-shaped-ochid design in
197	[forks-multi-user.md](forks-multi-user.md#per-user-bot-repos-via-url-shaped-ochid)
198	(the "ochid: bot-repo location qualifier" Todo): that entry
199	owns the published/URL half; this stage owns the local-path
200	half.
201	
202	- Rename the section: "workspace" is overloaded (cargo,
203	  VS Code, and jj itself has `jj workspace`) — vc-x1 is
204	  medium-agnostic. Candidate `[repos]`; settle at pickup.
205	- Path semantics for `work` / `bot`: an ordinary path —
206	  absolute, or relative to the directory containing the
207	  config file that states it (the standard file-relative
208	  rule; no leading-`/`-means-root special case). Docs
209	  recommend relative paths; absolute paths are allowed but
210	  discouraged — they commit one machine's layout.
211	- The literal identical-block invariant cannot survive
212	  file-relative values (the same bytes mean different dirs
213	  in each file); it is replaced by **resolved agreement** —
214	  canonicalize each side's declared pair and require both
215	  files to name the same two directories. The 0.75.0-3
216	  coherence preflight keeps its role, comparing reality
217	  instead of spelling.
218	- Side detection: the entry that resolves to the config's
219	  own directory names the side (`work = "."` → work repo).
220	  Repos need not be nested.
221	- ochid trailer prefixes become opaque repo labels resolved
222	  through the registry, not filesystem spellings: `/` and
223	  `/.claude` remain valid as historical labels for
224	  work/bot, so published trailers keep resolving; labels
225	  are intended to grow into URLs (the forks-multi-user
226	  design), making trailers clone-portable with no layout
227	  assumption.
228	- Committed identity vs local layout: a committed relative
229	  path is only honest while the repos travel together
230	  (nested, or siblings under a committed root). Non-nested
231	  layouts need the registry split — committed name/URL,
232	  per-machine local path in an uncommitted local file —
233	  designed here even if URL support lands later.
234	
235	We think this should run immediately after facade owns
236	topology (before de-gitify init): the schema is unreleased
237	and freshly adopted (one external workspace migrated at
238	0.75.0-2), so moving now means one migration wave instead
239	of two, and the init/clone rework (de-gitify init, the
240	template restructure) lands on the final schema instead of
241	being rewritten twice.
242

  verifies both repos' expected state up front — bot dir
  exists, both configs parse, `[workspace]` blocks identical
  — and on any finding it stops, prints everything known
  (both paths, both blocks), and changes nothing. Mid-flight
  surprises remain per-operation concerns (sync's
  stop-and-inspect, push's rollback); *entry* is gated at
  the one topology resolver the 0.75.0-3 sweep centralizes.

  config, so bot-side lookups fail with "missing

  broken commits out of history.

## Stage: repo registry

Decided 2026-07-24 (during the 0.75.0-4 review). The
`[workspace]` block becomes a repo registry — stable names
mapped to locations — and the root-anchored path grammar
(leading `/` = workspace root, pinned at 0.75.0-3) is
dropped. Complements the URL-shaped-ochid design in
[forks-multi-user.md](forks-multi-user.md#per-user-bot-repos-via-url-shaped-ochid)
(the "ochid: bot-repo location qualifier" Todo): that entry
owns the published/URL half; this stage owns the local-path
half.

- Rename the section: "workspace" is overloaded (cargo,
  VS Code, and jj itself has `jj workspace`) — vc-x1 is
  medium-agnostic. Candidate `[repos]`; settle at pickup.

  absolute, or relative to the directory containing the
  config file that states it (the standard file-relative
  rule; no leading-`/`-means-root special case). Docs
  recommend relative paths; absolute paths are allowed but
  discouraged — they commit one machine's layout.
- The literal identical-block invariant cannot survive
  file-relative values (the same bytes mean different dirs
  in each file); it is replaced by **resolved agreement** —
  canonicalize each side's declared pair and require both
  files to name the same two directories. The 0.75.0-3
  coherence preflight keeps its role, comparing reality
  instead of spelling.
- Side detection: the entry that resolves to the config's
  own directory names the side (`work = "."` → work repo).
  Repos need not be nested.
- ochid trailer prefixes become opaque repo labels resolved
  through the registry, not filesystem spellings: `/` and
  `/.claude` remain valid as historical labels for
  work/bot, so published trailers keep resolving; labels
  are intended to grow into URLs (the forks-multi-user
  design), making trailers clone-portable with no layout
  assumption.
- Committed identity vs local layout: a committed relative
  path is only honest while the repos travel together
  (nested, or siblings under a committed root). Non-nested
  layouts need the registry split — committed name/URL,
  per-machine local path in an uncommitted local file —
  designed here even if URL support lands later.

We think this should run immediately after facade owns
topology (before de-gitify init): the schema is unreleased
and freshly adopted (one external workspace migrated at
0.75.0-2), so moving now means one migration wave instead
of two, and the init/clone rework (de-gitify init, the
template restructure) lands on the final schema instead of
being rewritten twice.

I'm reacquainted. Your read is right, and here's the untangling:

## The structure: #1 is the program, #2–#8 are its stages

The 8 entries are **1 umbrella + 7 stages**, not 8 independent tasks. Todo #1 ("Refactor: typed jj facade → jj-lib in-process; end subprocess spawning") is the **program header** — it doesn't get executed itself; it's the short pointer to `notes/refactor-20260716.md`, which owns the execution order, per-stage design, and status. Its bullet says so: "The remaining stages are the individual 'Refactor stage: …' entries below." So #1's title names the *destination* of the whole program, and #6 is the stage that actually gets you there.

Three stages already shipped and were removed from the Todo list: **DRY facade** (0.73.0), **hygiene riders** (0.74.0), and **facade owns topology** — that last one just closed out (commit `dc14a42`, and there's a matching `## Done` entry), though the doc still says "In progress at 0.75.0" and could use a status touch-up. One more stage, **por → dual conversion**, lives in the backlog (todo-backlog.md #46) rather than the ranked list.

## What each remaining stage actually does, relative to "end spawning"

Only **one** stage eliminates spawning. The others are enablers or riders that travel in the same program:

- **#2 repo registry** — config schema work (`[workspace]` → a repo registry with ordinary paths and registry labels). Nothing to do with spawning; it's sequenced now so the freshly-adopted schema settles in one migration wave before init is reworked.
- **#3 de-gitify init** — replaces init's raw-**git** steps with a verified jj-only sequence. It removes *git* spawns but still spawns *jj*; it simplifies what #6 later has to lift in-process.
- **#4 split push.rs** — pure mechanical extraction (`push/state.rs`) so #6's rewrite of the stage bodies reviews cleanly.
- **#5 stateless push** — retires the push state file, deriving resume from repo reality. Shrinks/deletes much of what #4 isolates, which is why it runs between #4 and #6.
- **#6 jj-lib migration** — **this is the payload.** Facade internals and all mutations (commit, describe, bookmark ops, fetch, push) move in-process via jj-lib; `git init --bare` becomes a gix call. jj and git spawning end here. And because the lock acquisition now happens in our process, "the index-lock retry becomes ours" — we can catch, back off, and retry with real error types, which is the fix for the `bookmark-set` lock-race bug. That phrase in #6 isn't a different goal from #1's title; it's the concrete bug-fix dividend of doing #1.
- **#7 push body-intro validation** — small validation feature, sequenced after #6 only for program order.
- **#8 trapezoid close-out** — `push --merge`, a new feature that's easy *on* the in-process internals (a two-parent commit in one transaction), so it waits for #5 and #6.

## On your assumption

"Anything jj does we can do directly" is essentially correct — jj-lib is already a dependency (read-only commands use it today), and the doc's end state is exactly that. Three caveats the doc already records:

- **Working-copy snapshots**: spawned `jj` auto-snapshots `@`; in-process reads of `@` must snapshot explicitly, and a snapshot is an op-store *write* — so those reads move with the mutation lift, not before.

Quick scope check done — the DRY facade already consolidated things nicely (spawn sites are down to `jj.rs` facade internals plus ~12 mutation sites in `init.rs`, `push.rs`, `repo_utils.rs`, `clone.rs`). My read on each stage:

**Likely single-step** (one Work commit + close-out):

- **#4 split push.rs** — pure mechanical extraction, and it was already built *once* as a single commit (0.72.0-1, parked on `support-trapezoid-commits`). Replaying or redoing it is one commit almost by definition.
- **#7 push body-intro validation** — one validation function, one clear error message, tests. The smallest stage in the program.
- **#3 de-gitify init** — borderline, but I lean single-step: the replacement sequence is already verified on a scratch run (the doc lists the exact five jj commands), and it's a swap of one flow inside `init.rs::push_repo`. If it grows a second rung it'd be test-fixture cleanup, not design.

**Clearly multi-step**:

- **#2 repo registry** — same weight class as facade-owns-topology (which took a ~5-rung ladder): section rename, new path semantics, the identical-block invariant replaced by resolved agreement, side detection by resolution, ochid labels, plus migrating both live configs and docs. I'd guess 3–5 rungs.
- **#5 stateless push** — reworking resume derivation, deleting `PushState` persistence, the stale-state verifier arms, `--restart`/`--from`, and the `.gitignore` check, each of which wants its own reviewable commit. ~3–4 rungs.
- **#6 jj-lib migration** — the biggest by far, and the doc already hints it: reads-lift, mutations-lift (workspace/transaction/op-store), the retry loop, the gix `init --bare`, *plus* the op-store-coexistence risk that wants a spike/compat-check rung before committing to the approach. This could honestly be **multiple cycles**, not just multiple rungs — reads-migration as one `X.Y.Z` and mutations as another would be a defensible split.
- **#8 trapezoid close-out** — the merge commit itself is trivial, but the ochid multi-stamping, teaching `validate-desc` + both push sanity verifiers the new legal shape, and the docs ride-along make it 3+ rungs.

So the split is roughly **3 small (#3, #4, #7) vs 4 real ladders (#2, #5, #6, #8)**, with #6 possibly deserving promotion to two cycles. If you're thinking of handling them differently: the three small ones are candidates for quick single-commit cycles (or even bundling — #4 is a natural prep rung *inside* whatever cycle starts #5, since #5 immediately shrinks what #4 extracted), while the four big ones each keep the full ladder treatment.

The plain version: three of the seven are one-sitting jobs; four are proper projects, and the jj-lib one is the project of projects.

content.text:
Your consolidation and the version tangle are actually the same story, so let me take them together.

## The 4-task consolidation: I endorse it, the pairings match the doc's own dependency notes

- **2+3** — the doc already says registry runs "right after facade owns topology... so de-gitify init builds on it." De-gitify as the registry cycle's last rung is natural: it's a one-commit swap of an already-verified sequence.
- **4+5** — the doc literally warns "the stateless push stage may shrink or delete much of what the extraction isolated." Doing the extraction as rung 1 of the stateless cycle means the extraction and its shrinkage land in one reviewable arc instead of two cycles that partially undo each other. This is the best pairing of the three.
- **6 as-is** — right, though keep the option open of it becoming two cycles (reads-lift, then mutations-lift) once the op-store-coexistence spike answers the version-skew question.
- **7+8** — #7's "after jj-lib" was only program order, not a dependency, so pulling it in as rung 1 of the trapezoid cycle is fine; both are push-shape/validation work on the same files.

On promoting #1 to `## In Progress`: reasonable, and honest — the program *is* in progress (three stages shipped). The one convention wrinkle: In Progress blocks normally carry a per-cycle ladder with `X.Y.Z-N` rungs. I'd structure it as the program block holding the 4-task sequence as its "ladder" (each rung = one future cycle, no version numbers yet), and when a task opens, its real versioned ladder appears under it. That keeps "In Progress = what's underway" true at both granularities.

## The version situation: abandon 0.72.0, harvest the branch, document the gap

Here's my read of the state: `main` sits at 0.71.0; `refactor-vc-x1` forked from it and ran 0.73.0 → 0.75.0; `support-trapezoid-commits` also forked from it carrying the parked 0.72.0-0/-1. The two branches are siblings — 0.72.0 was allocated to a cycle that paused, and the refactor program skipped over it.

You're right that rebasing refactor-vc-x1 onto support-trapezoid-commits is silly — and it's worse than silly: the parked extraction targets *pre-refactor* `push.rs`, which the DRY-facade and topology stages have since churned. The parked work is stale relative to the code it would sit under, not just awkwardly numbered.

My recommendation:

- **Treat support-trapezoid-commits as a quarry, not a branch.** Its durable value is already extracted: the design decisions live in the refactor doc's trapezoid stage (the 2026-07-20 "Design points settled" block), and your 0.72.0 ladder above is a ready-made template for the new task #4's ladder. The 0.72.0-0 chore-open commit is worthless (stale version bump + todo state). The 0.72.0-1 extraction *might* rebase cleanly onto the refactor tip when task #2 (split+stateless) opens — try `jj rebase` then, and if push.rs has drifted too far, redo it with the parked diff as reference. Either way, re-describe it under the new cycle's version. Then delete the bookmark.
- **Accept the 0.72.0 hole and document it.** Versions here are cheap cycle labels, not released artifacts — a documented skip is harmless, while the alternative (renumbering the refactor branch's 0.73–0.75 down by one) means rewriting history that's already cross-linked through chores, TODO Done entries, and ochids. One line in versioning.md (or the refactor doc's split-push stage): "0.72.0 was allocated to the parked trapezoid close-out cycle and abandoned; the stage was redone at 0.7X.0." Future archaeologists get the decoder ring; nothing rewrites.

Worth noticing: this whole tangle is a *live specimen* of your existing Todo "Version-number protocol is fragile — versions are baked in before the change lands." The 0.72.0 hole exists precisely because a version was assigned to work that didn't land in sequence. I'd add this episode as a concrete example bullet on that Todo — it's better evidence than the hypothetical Linux-merge scenario it currently cites.

**The plain version:** your 4-task plan is good and I'd adopt it as-is. Don't rebase anything onto the parked branch — mine it for parts later and delete it. Let 0.72.0 be a number that never shipped, write one line saying why, and note that this annoyance is exactly the bug your "versions are fragile" Todo predicted.

13. **sync follow-up: push preflight in-process; drop
    `--check`; revisit push auto-rollback.** Push's preflight
    shells out to `vc-x1 sync --check` — a verify-only pass
    that is both racy (remote can move before the user's
    later apply) and not actually read-only (jj's fetch
    auto-ffs tracked bookmarks). Follow-up to the 0.67.0
    single-mode sync cycle.

      nothing invokes it.
    - Apply the stop-on-error + `vc-x1 revert` philosophy to
      push's commit-stage rollback (today it auto-runs
      `jj op restore`, hiding the evidence).
14. **validate-numbering: rename the pair, check all
    sequence-managed notes files generically.** `validate-todo`
    / `fix-todo` only operate on the single file passed, so a
    renumber slip in `bugs.md`, `todo-backlog.md`, or
    `TODO.md`'s `## Ideas` section passes unnoticed — too weak
    for a pre-commit gate. Prereq for the pre-commit doc
    validators (Todo "pre-commit: single rule ...").
    - Rename the pair: `validate-todo` → `validate-numbering`,
      `fix-todo` → `fix-numbering` — they validate numbered-
      sequence integrity, not todos specifically.
    - Generic detection: for every `#…#` section, validate the
      column-0 `^\d+\.␠` entries form a contiguous 1..N run.
      Drops the Todo/Bugs special-casing; auto-covers
      `## Ideas` and any new numbered section. Keep the
      column-0 anchor so indented sub-lists aren't counted.

      files (`TODO.md`, `todo-backlog.md`, `bugs.md`) so the
      no-arg pre-commit run covers them all. Fixed rather than
      a `notes/**.md` walk because prose docs
      (`cycle-protocol.md`, design notes) carry ordinary
      numbered lists that aren't managed sequences — a walk
      would false-positive (markdown renders `1. 1. 1.` as
      1-2-3, a legitimate prose pattern).
    - Override args follow the `--init-from` convention:
      positional files/dirs (a dir → its `*.md`) plus an
      `@<file>` manifest, additive — for ad-hoc validation of
      a specific file.
    - Add wrapper-level tests while restructuring: the analyze
      cores are covered (`todo_helpers` 15 tests,

      unexercised.
    - Open: revisit fixed-vs-glob at implementation if the
      fixed list proves annoying to maintain.
15. **pre-commit: single rule (no docs skip) + doc validators.**
    The pre-commit (cargo cycle: fmt/clippy/test/install) only
    checks code, so it's "skip-able for purely-docs commits" —
    but that exception is exactly where checks slip (skipped on
    0.62.0-7/-8 until caught). (Since 0.69.0-3 push's
    `preflight` no longer re-runs the cargo cycle — vc-x1
    assumes nothing about repo contents — so the pre-commit is
    the *only* gate, strengthening the no-skip case.)

      Work review on every commit. (docs: AGENTS.md Cycle
      Protocol summary + cycle-protocol.md per-commit-flow.)
    - Enrich the pre-commit so it's meaningful on docs commits:
      add the doc validators — `validate-numbering` (its own

97	phase in the version suffix — the **final identifier `0` marks

## Unique per commit (preference, not requirement)

Our general notion is that the version-of-record should change
on **every commit**, so a built or running artifact identifies
the exact commit it came from.

- This is a preference, **not** a hard requirement. A project
  following the cycle protocol may bump less often — once per
  cycle, only at release, and so on. Record the choice in
  [Recording the version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record)
  if it differs.
- It is achievable because the cycle's versions (below) are
  **pre-assignable**, unlike the git SHA, which a commit cannot
  contain (see the cycle protocol's
  [Commits backfill](cycle-protocol.md#commits-backfill)).

## Step numbering

The cycle (Preparation -> Work -> Close-out; see
[cycle-protocol.md](cycle-protocol.md)) encodes each commit's
phase in the version suffix — the **final identifier `0` marks
a Preparation**:

- `X.Y.Z-0` — Preparation
- `X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, … — Work commits
- `X.Y.Z` — Close-out (bare version, no suffix)

**Preparation is optional.** A lightweight cycle — no ladder,
no setup commit — skips `-0` and starts at `-1` (its first
Work commit). The same holds at every level: a sub-cycle
needing no Preparation omits its `.0` (see Nesting). One that
grows a Preparation later adds the `0` step without
renumbering siblings.

Disambiguation:

- `-10` — Work commit #10 (final identifier `10`), not a
  Preparation.
- `-1.0` — Preparation of the `-1` sub-cycle (final
  identifier `0`).

**Nesting.** Sub-cycles append another level, recursively:

- `X.Y.Z-3.0` — Preparation of the `-3` sub-cycle
- `X.Y.Z-3.1`, `X.Y.Z-3.2` — its Work
- `X.Y.Z-3` — its Close-out
- `X.Y.Z-3.1.0` — Preparation of the `-3.1` sub-sub-cycle

Bump the version-of-record at the start of each phase, so the
active phase is recorded — and, per the preference above,
every commit carries a distinct version.

shared protocol set — `AGENTS.md` (root), `notes/cycle-protocol.md`,

## In Progress

When a `## Todo` item is picked up, its text **moves** here
(never copied — one home per text). The picked-up task is a
`###` heading; a multi-cycle program adds one level — the
program is the `###` and its current stage a `####` (headings
give the current work durable anchors, which numbered Todo
entries can't). The problem overview is followed by the
"plan" — a bulleted list of the development "ladder". Each
rung is prepended with its commit reference — a literal
`[[N]]` placeholder until the commit is pushed, then
backfilled to a real file-local `[[n]]` ref (same pattern as
the chores As-built rungs):
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-0 blah (done)
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-1 blah blah (current)
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-2 blah blah blah
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y close-out and validation

### Refactor: typed jj facade → jj-lib in-process; end subprocess spawning

Version-control operations were ~30 hand-rolled `run("jj", …)`
spawns plus every mutation, with per-module private wrappers
and raw-git vestiges in init — stderr parsing instead of typed
errors, and jj's single-attempt index-lock acquisition (the
push `bookmark-set` lock race in [bugs.md](notes/bugs.md))
can't be retried where it fails. A multi-ladder program; the
staged plan, design detail, and the eight absorbed former
Todos live in
[refactor-20260716.md](notes/refactor-20260716.md).

- Shipped: DRY facade (0.73.0), hygiene riders (0.74.0),
  facade owns topology (0.75.0).
- Remaining, as four cycles (adjacent stages consolidated
  2026-07-24 — small stages ride as rungs of their
  neighbor; the doc owns per-stage design):
  - repo registry, with de-gitify init as its last rung
    (current, below)
  - split push.rs + stateless push (Todo #1)
  - jj-lib migration (Todo #2)
  - push body-intro validation + trapezoid close-out
    (Todo #3)

#### Refactor stage: repo registry

Drop the root-anchored `[workspace]` path grammar: values
become ordinary paths (relative to the config file's dir, or
absolute — allowed but docs discourage), resolved agreement
replaces the identical-block invariant, ochid prefixes become
registry labels (URLs later — the local-path half of the Todo
"ochid: bot-repo location qualifier"), and the section is
renamed ("workspace" is overloaded — jj itself has
`jj workspace`). Decided 2026-07-24; see
[the stage](notes/refactor-20260716.md#stage-repo-registry).
First so the schema settles in one migration wave; de-gitify
init rides as the last rung — a one-commit swap to the
verified jj-only sequence
([the stage](notes/refactor-20260716.md#stage-de-gitify-init)).

Plan (informal until the cycle opens):

- rename `[workspace]` (candidate `[repos]`); file-relative
  path semantics; side detection by self-resolution
- resolved-agreement preflight replaces the identical-block
  invariant
- ochid prefixes become registry labels (`/` and `/.claude`
  stay valid as historical labels for work/bot)
- migrate both live configs + docs
- de-gitify init (last rung)
- close-out and validation

content.text:
Thoughts — I agree on both counts, with the reasoning and a few ripples to confirm:

**Dropping "stage:" — yes, and it's better than cosmetic.** The convention says a ladder rung's title *is* the commit title (rung ↔ chores header ↔ commit, verbatim). The three shipped close-outs are literally `refactor: DRY jj facade`, `refactor: hygiene riders`, `refactor: facade owns topology` — no "stage" in them. So `refactor: repo registry` etc. isn't just shorter, it's the anticipated close-out title, which makes the rung greppable against `git log` the day it lands. The old form was never going to survive contact with the commit anyway.

Ripple to confirm: "change *all*" — I'd sweep the three `## Todo` entry titles (**Refactor stage: split push.rs + stateless push** → **refactor: split push.rs + stateless push**) and the `#### Refactor stage: repo registry` heading (→ `#### refactor: repo registry`) to match. Same argument: the `####` heading is a commit-recording heading, so it should carry the anticipated close-out title exactly, like a chores `##` header does. The word "stage" survives only in the refactor doc's `## Stage: …` section names, where it's structural, not a title.

**Pre-assigned versions 0.76.0–0.79.0 — fine, and not a repeat of the 0.72.0 mistake.** The 0.72.0 hole hurt because the version was baked into *commits* (immutable). TODO.md is mutable — if jj-lib splits into two cycles, or an unrelated cycle claims 0.76.0, fixing the ladder is a one-line edit. Pre-assignment in a planning file buys readability at trivial maintenance cost. I'd hedge exactly one rung: jj-lib migration already carries a "may split into two cycles" note, so expect 0.78.0/0.79.0 to be the likeliest lines to shift.

**The [[X]]s: there's no X convention — those rungs just get backfilled now.** The existing pattern is `[[N]]` placeholder → real file-local `[[n]]`. The three shipped rungs should carry real refs immediately: new TODO.md slots pointing at the close-out commits in the chores commit-ref shape (12-hex URL + 40-hex title). I already have them: `b5e40e7458b8` (DRY facade), `946dc964b75c` (hygiene riders), `dc14a421d850` (facade owns topology). Note these coexist with the Done entries' existing refs to chores-14 *sections* — different targets, different slots, both legitimate.

**One honesty check on "the X's are real":** all these SHAs live on `refactor-vc-x1`, not `main` — the backfill rule says SHAs are stable only on a permanent branch. They're "real" only because we've committed to never rebasing this branch (merge-only landing). I'm fine with that, but it means `refactor-vc-x1` is now formally a long-lived branch in the protocol's sense, and I'd say so in one line where we backfill — otherwise a future reader sees a rule violation instead of a decision. Same reasoning legitimizes backfilling the six chores-14 `[[N]]`s (0.75.0-0 through 0.75.0, → slots [14]–[19]).

So when you give the word: program ladder as you sketched (with `refactor:` titles and real refs for the three shipped rungs), the "stage" sweep across Todo titles + the `####` heading, the one-line long-lived-branch note, and the chores-14 backfill.

LG, where should this land, we can make it part of 0.76.0-0 or 0.75.1, if we make this 0.75.1
we should probably move "current todo",  "refactor: repo registry", back to todo #1 and renumber.

I mildly lean to making it 0.75.1, your thoughts no actions?

As a side note, this this entire refactor set should have been 0.73.1 .. 0.73.7.
One other thing, I really like seeing the version easily, historically we put it in
the title but have decided that it's not durable enough to be there. So for awhile
it's can be found in Cargo.toml but that means in gitk I have to click on the change
list then click on Cargo.toml to see what the version is. By having:

  "- Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock: version x.y.z-n"

at the top the description "file list". That way it's always visible in gitk's
"main" window and I don't have to specifically browse the list in main window or
select Cargo.toml in the file list.  So, think we need to codify that in our,
something you suggested but I said AGENTS.md is too long. So I was wrong and now
I'm thinking we codify it in cycle-protocol.md so as to no grow AGENTS.md make
do codify it.

So as above thoughts, no actions.

content.text:
Thoughts on all three, no actions:

**0.75.1 — agree.** This restructure is a standalone planning/bookkeeping change, not the opening move of the repo-registry cycle, and giving it its own version keeps 0.76.0-0 clean to do what a prep commit is for: the actual pickup. It also lands the chores-14 backfill promptly instead of letting it ride. And yes, your consequence follows from the intro we just wrote ("moves here when picked up"): if nothing is picked up yet, `#### refactor: repo registry` goes back to Todo #1 with the others renumbering 2–4, and the ladder rung's marker changes from "(current, below)" to "(Todo #1)". The `###` program block itself stays in In Progress — the *program* genuinely is in progress (three cycles shipped); only the stage's pickup hasn't happened. As a lightweight docs-only cycle, 0.75.1 can skip `-0` per versioning.md — possibly a single bare `0.75.1` commit; the version bump touches Cargo.toml so the cargo cycle runs regardless.

**"Should have been 0.73.1..0.73.7"** — I see the appeal: the program is one arc, and minor-per-cycle spends seven minors on what is conceptually one refactor. A patch-per-cycle-within-a-program scheme (program claims `X.Y`, cycles take `X.Y.1..n`) would encode program membership right in the version. Two counterpoints: the current cadence is uniform and decision-free (every cycle bumps minor — no "is this part of a program?" judgment call at prep time), and vc-x1 is unreleased so minors are free. I'd not renumber anything now, but this is a genuinely good input for the "Version-number protocol is fragile" Todo — it's a second, independent pressure on the same question (what identifies a cycle's commits), worth a bullet there when we next touch it.

**Version-first-bullet in the commit body — agree, and cycle-protocol.md is the right home.** The rule as I'd state it: the body's file list opens with `- Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock: version X.Y.Z-N` — always first, so the version is visible in gitk's message pane without opening the file list. It fits the existing conventions perfectly: titles stay version-free (the durability decision stands), the file-by-file bullet for the bump already exists on most commits since vc-x1 bumps every commit — this just pins its position and phrasing. Home: the [Commit description] section of cycle-protocol.md's per-commit flow. One consequence to accept: cycle-protocol.md is in the byte-identical shared doc set, so this is another intentional local divergence that joins the pending family fan-out (same path as the per-commit chores convention — the "Shared-doc sync" Todo #15 pattern; this edit would ride the same sync). Given the family already has a queued sync, growing it by one settled convention is cheap.

So my proposed 0.75.1 content when you say go: move repo registry back to Todo #1 + renumber, adjust the ladder marker, add the version-first-bullet convention to cycle-protocol.md, and — if you want it in the same commit — the fragile-versions Todo gains the program-numbering thought as a bullet.

## Per-commit flow

Every commit (Preparation, each Work commit, Close-out) goes
through:

1. **Mark this commit `(current)`** as the first edit in
   `TODO.md > ## In Progress` (`TODO.md` is at the repo
   root).
2. **Do the work** (see [Iterative work](#iterative-work)
   for the loop-and-squash technique).
3. **Flip this commit `(current)` → `(done)`** in `## In
   Progress` — before the cargo cycle and the commit.
4. **Validate the artifact** — a medium-specific step, skip-able
   for notes-only commits, mandatory at close-out. For the Rust
   example the cargo cycle is:
   1. `cargo fmt`
   2. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
   3. `cargo test`
   4. `cargo install --path . --locked`
   5. (re-test if anything substantive changed)
5. **Work review.** Stop *before* writing any description;
   tell the user "ready to commit." The user reviews the
   changes and we iterate until complete.
6. **Write the commit description** — see
   [Commit description](#commit-description).
7. **Commit Description review.** Show the title + body
   and stop. The user reviews the description. Iterate.
8. **Commit.** `jj commit -m "title" -m "body" -R .` for
   the work repo, `-R .claude` for the bot repo (`-R` last
   keeps the verb visible):

   ```
   jj commit -m \
   "<type>: <short description>" \
   -m "<intro paragraph>

   - file1: gist
   - file2: gist

   ochid: /.claude/<chid>" \
   -R .
   ```

**Two overrides apply:**

- **Deviation or question** — any time the work deviates
  from the agreed plan, or a question arises, stop and
  surface it; don't push through.
- **ESC-ESC** — the user can interrupt at any point to pull
  a review or question forward.

## Commit description

[Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/):

```
<type>: <short description>
```

Titles carry **no trailing `(<version>)` suffix**. The
version-of-record — where it lives and its bump cadence, see
[versioning.md](versioning.md) — is useful for confirming
you're running the version you're testing, not a per-commit
title marker. We think per-commit version-in-title is
unstable on large projects: many changes are in flight
simultaneously, and a
version is only stable once merged into the main repo — so
titles don't carry one.

### Title

- ≤50 chars total.
- Common types: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `test`,
  `docs`, `chore`.
- Favor terse phrasings.
- **Distinct per step** — each of a cycle's commits gets its
  own descriptive title (no shared cycle title with a step
  marker). Share a greppable stem across the cycle's titles
  (e.g. `ring buffer`) so `git log --grep` collects them; the
  chores section header matches the close-out title. See
  AGENTS.md
  [Conventional-commit shape](../AGENTS.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--chores--commit).

### Body

[Prose form](../AGENTS.md#prose-form) (intro + bullets),
wrap ≤72. Bullet content differs per repo:

- **Work-repo body**: file-by-file. One bullet per file
  changed (file plus a one-line gist). Sub-bullets for
  files with multiple distinct changes:

  ```
  - path/to/file1
    - first distinct change
    - second distinct change, wrapping to next line
       with continuation indented 5
  ```

  The file-by-file list is the source of truth for the
  cycle's mechanical change record. Chores carries the
  narrative + design, not a copy of it. Promote any
  "why" beyond one sentence to a chores `###` subsection.

- **Bot-repo (`.claude`) body**: bullets describe
  in-session activity rather than work-repo changes.

### Trailer

`ochid:` as the last line of the body — see
[Cross-repo linking (ochid trailers)](../AGENTS.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)
in AGENTS.md for the convention.

For breaking changes, use the hyphenated `BREAKING-CHANGE:`
trailer key. `BREAKING CHANGE:` (with a space) is the only
space-separated key the Conventional Commits spec allows; the
hyphenated form is also valid and avoids the space ambiguity.

## Reviewing changes

Work review looks at the **uncommitted working-copy diff**,
on the way to commit. The user opens diffs in their
editor (Zed, VSCode); jj commands are for terminal:

- `jj diff` — working-copy diff (uncommitted)
- `jj diff -r @-` — diff of the previous commit
- `jj diff --from <X> --to <Y>` — any two revisions
- `jj show -r <X>` — description + diff for one rev

Don't `jj edit -r @-` to view a past commit — that marks
it mutable and shifts `@`; use `jj diff -r @-` or
`jj show -r @-`.

See [Sub-cycle ladders](#sub-cycle-ladders) for the
close-out squash recipe and recovery; revset primitives
are in [`jj-tips.md`](jj-tips.md#revsets).

## Pushing

### Policy
